lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: understand that plants respond to stimuli
describe the geotropic and phototropic responses of roots and stems
understand the role of auxin in the phototropic response of stems

primer.text: You know plants need light for photosynthesis and water from the soil. This note explains how rooted organisms still manage to steer themselves: shoots grow toward light and away from gravity, roots do the opposite, and a chemical called auxin runs the whole steering system. Learn the tropism vocabulary here — it is heavily examined.

modules.title: Tropisms: directional growth toward and away
modules.opening: Plants cannot walk away from problems, so they grow their way out instead. Directional growth toward or away from light and gravity is called a tropism: shoots climb toward light and against gravity, while roots push downward with gravity and away from light, anchoring the plant and reaching water.
keyPoints: Plants grow in response to stimuli such as light and gravity.
Directional growth responses to light and gravity are named tropisms.
Growth toward the stimulus is positive; growth away is negative.
Shoots show positive phototropism and negative geotropism.
Roots show positive geotropism and negative phototropism.

low.restatement: Shoots bend toward light and upward against gravity; roots drive downward with gravity and away from light.
low.analogy: A plant is a two-way traveller — its top chases sunshine while its bottom hunts deep water.
low.examPointer: Learn the four pairings in the table: shoot or root, with light or gravity, each carrying its sign.

medium.restatement: Tropisms couple a directional stimulus to growth direction: phototropism orients shoots for photosynthesis while geotropism anchors roots and aims them at soil water and minerals.
medium.analogy: Think of a hotel with two concierges — one steers guests toward the bright lobby, the other toward the underground car park.
medium.examPointer: Definitions earn marks: name the tropism, the organ and the sign — 'positive phototropism of shoots' is a complete answer.

modules.title: Auxin: the chemistry of the phototropic bend
sourceHeadings: The Role of Auxin in Phototropism
modules.opening: Auxin is the plant's growth coordinator. Made in the shoot tips, it moves just behind the tip where it makes existing cells elongate; the more auxin, the faster the stretch. When light strikes one side, auxin collects on the shaded side, those cells lengthen faster, and the shoot bends toward the light.
keyPoints: Auxins are plant growth regulators coordinating directional growth.
Auxin is manufactured in shoot tips and moves downward to the zone just behind, where cell division happens.
Auxin makes existing cells elongate; higher auxin means faster elongation.
Even light gives an even auxin spread, so shoots grow straight.
One-sided light concentrates auxin on the shaded side, whose cells lengthen faster and bend the shoot toward the light.

low.restatement: Tip-made auxin pools on the shaded side, stretching those cells faster, so the shoot curves sunward.
low.analogy: Like a rowing boat turning — the shaded-side cells are the rowers pulling harder on one side.
low.examPointer: Say cell elongation, never cell division — the exam hint penalises answers claiming new cells appear.

medium.restatement: Auxin's gradient across the shoot is the mechanism: uniform light gives uniform elongation, unilateral light gives an elongation gap that bends the organ.
medium.analogy: A bimetallic strip bends because one metal expands more; a shoot bends because one side elongates more.
medium.examPointer: Quote the dose relationship — the more auxin, the faster the elongation — when explaining the bend.

glossary.definition: A directional growth response of a plant toward (positive) or away (negative) from a stimulus such as light or gravity.
The directional growth response to light; positive in shoots, negative in roots.
The directional growth response to gravity; positive in roots, negative in shoots.
A plant growth regulator made in shoot tips that makes existing cells elongate faster where it accumulates.
